B. Wajnryb, Relations in the mapping class group (2006), Chapter 8. The source of the fixed-positive-word quotient question and the stated Perron–Vannier regular-neighborhood chain embedding theorem.
D. Auroux, Mapping class group factorizations and symplectic 4-manifolds: some open problems (2006), Chapter 9. Distinguishes strict Hurwitz moves from simultaneous global conjugation.

R. I. Baykur, N. Monden and J. Van Horn-Morris, Positive factorizations of mapping classes (2017). Theorem A supplies the classical maximum length 40 for a positive nonseparating factorization of the genus-two, one-boundary twist.
J. González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups (2011). The faithful Artin free-group representation and positive braid monoid embedding are established tools used by the proof.

M. Matsumoto, A presentation of mapping class groups in terms of Artin groups and geometric monodromy of singularities (2000). Credits the classical genus-two quotient presentation. The original 1997 institutional manuscript is also cited in the paper.

Y. Sato, 2-Spheres of Square −1 and the Geography of Genus-2 Lefschetz Fibrations (2008). The earlier geography result already gives the length spectrum 20, 30, 40 in the corresponding square−1-section, no-reducible-fibre setting.

E. A. Elrifai and H. R. Morton, Algorithms for positive braids (1994). Reports Casson’s general crossing assertion on page 496, without a proof or separate Casson reference. The six-strand certificate is additional evidence for that known assertion.
Alec Kriebel (2026). Fixed-generator positive factorizations in Wajnryb's Artin A5 quotient. Zenodo version 1.0, 3 October 2026. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23124601.

J. Byszewski, Dévissage for local deformation functors, Oberwolfach Reports 54/2008, pp. 3038–3040. The unrestricted question on page 3039 is distinct from Theorem 3, which adds component-prorepresentability hypotheses.

J. Byszewski, Cohomological aspects of equivariant deformation theory, Utrecht Ph.D. thesis (2009). Question 6.4.4 and the separate conditional result provide the thesis formulation of the same question.

J. Byszewski, Deformation functors of local actions, arXiv:1112.0352v1 (2011). Supplies the deformation-category, actual fixed-functor, restriction/induction and tangent-cohomology framework. Question 4.4 and Remark 4.5 keep the unrestricted and conditional formulations separate.

J. Byszewski and G. Cornelissen, Which weakly ramified group actions admit a universal formal deformation? (2009). The additive action and exceptional involution pathology are prior work. Proposition 4.1 gives the parameter-shift conjugacy; Proposition 6.1 gives the injection collision, from which all-recipient tangent collapse follows by naturality.

F. Vivaldi, joint work with J. A. G. Roberts, Maps over finite fields: integrability and reversibility, OWR 54/2004, pp.2944–2945. The broad birational existence assertion and point-weighted T/p statistic. The later genus-one heuristic and Conjecture 2 use different scope.

A. Ostafe and I. E. Shparlinski, On the degree growth in some polynomial dynamical systems and nonlinear pseudorandom number generators, arXiv:0902.3884v3 (2009), §2.1. The older triangular polynomial family contains the displayed map after exchanging coordinates.

A. R. Booker, S. D. Cohen, N. Sutherland and T. Trudgian, Primitive values of quadratic polynomials in a finite field, arXiv:1803.01435v2 (2018), §2. Classical primitive-value character framework, equations (5)–(6) and Lemma 1.

L. Menici and C. Pehlivan, Average r-rank Artin conjecture, Acta Arithmetica 174(3) (2016), 255–276. The unconditional shifted-prime mean, with r=m=1 in Lemma 2. This is not the fixed-base primitive-root conjecture.

J.-M. Deshouillers and M. Hassani, A note on the distribution function of φ(p−1)/(p−1), J. Aust. Math. Soc.93 (2012), 77–83; online 16 January 2013. The continuous shifted-prime scalar empirical law, associated with Kátai; Proposition 2.1 and its m=2 application.

S. Aivazidis and E. Sofos, On the distribution of the density of maximal order elements in general linear groups, arXiv:1308.5701v2 (2014). The n=1 mean and continuous law in Theorems 1.1(i) and 1.3(i), including the prime/prime-power relation in §6. Standard Dirichlet, prime number theorem and Siegel–Walfisz inputs are explicitly used.

J. A. G. Roberts, Order and symmetry in birational difference equations and their signatures over finite phase spaces, Vigo proceedings (2011), pp.213–221. Printed p.220, reference 9, authenticates the unresolved four-author 2011 preprint citation. The cited preprint body remains unrecovered.
